copy.d030: Google Home, Google TV, Chromecast and Roku: what each one does
copy.d031: Google Home is not the same thing as Google TV
copy.d032: The Google Home app is used to set up and manage compatible smart-home and Cast devices. Chromecast is a family of streaming devices and casting technology; Chromecast with Google TV adds a browsable TV interface. Google's newer Google TV Streamer is a separate 4K streaming device, with Google TV recommendations and smart-home features. If you searched for “what to watch on Google Home,” you probably need a content recommendation, not instructions to control a smart home.
copy.d033: Google TV can search across supported apps, surface personalized picks and maintain a cross-service watchlist. Its “Freeplay” and third-party free-TV offers depend on the market. MatchApp Ai offers a complementary route: describe whether you want a light comedy, an intense mystery or a quick documentary before you search a specific device's supported apps.
copy.d039: Roku device versus The Roku Channel
copy.d040: A Roku TV or streaming player is the device and operating-system experience. The Roku Channel is Roku's own free, ad-supported catalog, separate from the other streaming apps a Roku device can open. Roku's Live TV Channel Guide also surfaces channels, but its supported listings vary by country.
copy.d041: According to Roku's official support, The Roku Channel is available through Roku devices, web and mobile in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom; in Mexico, support is limited to Roku streaming devices. copy.d047: Amazon Fire TV and Prime Video are different products
copy.d048: Fire TV is the interface and device family. Prime Video is a content service that can be accessed through it. Fire TV's Find, Free, Live and My Stuff areas help with video search, free programming and watchlists; the titles surfaced can depend on installed applications and subscriptions. Alexa voice search is a Fire TV feature, not a MatchApp Ai integration.
copy.d049: If you use Fire TV, start with “what movie should I watch tonight?” and specify tone, format, region and whether you prefer a free, subscription, rental or purchase route. Then search for the chosen title inside the supported provider application.
copy.d051: Apple TV 4K, the Apple TV app and Apple TV subscription are not interchangeable
copy.d052: Apple TV 4K is a hardware box with apps. The Apple TV app is a viewing and recommendation interface available on multiple kinds of devices, and Apple's original-content subscription is a separate offering. Other subscriptions and rentals may still cost money. A title visible in an app does not necessarily come included with another service's plan.

copy.d058: Free TV channels: the alternatives people often overlook
copy.d059: Free, ad-supported streaming television (often called FAST) offers scheduled live channels or on-demand catalogs funded by advertising. It is different from a paid subscription, an individual rental and over-the-air broadcast TV. “Free app” does not guarantee every title inside an ecosystem is free.

copy.d113: Questions people ask about streaming devices and channels
copy.d114: Can Google Home or Chromecast recommend movies?
copy.d115: Google TV offers recommendations, and Google Home supports compatible home and casting controls. The features differ by product. MatchApp Ai helps with an independent mood-based shortlist but does not use your Google Home account or control your Chromecast.
copy.d116: Can I watch The Roku Channel on a Roku device in Brazil?
copy.d117: Do not assume so. Roku's official eligibility statement names specific regions and device limitations and does not list Brazil as a supported Roku Channel country. Other services on a Brazilian Roku device may still be available separately.
copy.d118: Are Samsung TV Plus, LG Channels and Plex actually free?
copy.d119: They provide free, ad-supported content on supported products or in supported markets. Some ecosystems separately offer paid rentals or other paid features. Always verify the exact service, market and title.
copy.d120: Is the Apple TV app the same as buying an Apple TV 4K?
copy.d121: No. The app is available on multiple device types, while Apple TV 4K is dedicated hardware. A subscription or rental remains separate from the hardware purchase.
copy.d122: Can MatchApp Ai send a title directly to my TV?
copy.d123: No direct casting, TV remote or proprietary-device integration is claimed here. Use MatchApp Ai for discovery, then open the licensed streaming provider on the device you already use.
